text:
The Devils arrive on a three-game winning streak, the latest a 5-4 overtime win over STL that Jesper Bratt finished. They're 4-1-0 in their last five. The Islanders are 2-3-0 over the same stretch and lost 5-3 to CAR on Nov 5, with Ryan Pulock, Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie out. With Maccelli gone, Bo Horvat has moved onto his spot beside Cizikas and Holmstrom, and Simon Holmstrom is up to 20:55 a night from 15:43. NJD also has a score to settle: NYI beat them 6-0 on Oct 3.

Our numbers favor the Devils (3.32 expected goals tonight to 2.74). At five on five, NJD has taken 59% of the expected goals, a measure of chance quality, against 50% for NYI. NJD's power play (0.79 expected goals a game) meets a penalty kill allowing 0.86, and NYI takes 4.5 penalties a game, which keeps feeding opponents' power plays. In net, projected starter Connor Hellebuyck sits at -0.5 goals saved above expected this season, while Ilya Sorokin is at +5.6 and finished +22.3 last year.

Jack Hughes is our top scoring threat at 40% to score and 77% to get a point, and he leads the Devils with the top power-play role. Arseny Gritsyuk has 10 points in his last 10 games, and the chances back it, though we'd expect him to cool. For NYI, Horvat is the likeliest scorer at 36%.
